messages:
maya: quick q: can we ship an operator-delegation flow for config edits with limited TTL + a shadow-apply mode? thinking about on-call needing to flip routing/quota in emergencies without a full PR cycle :thinking_face:

jonah: we have partial support via temp-overrides today but it's console-only and lacks TTL + dry-run. what exactly are you proposing?

maya: sketch: 1) shadow-apply that simulates decisions against prod traffic, 2) operator-delegate that mints a scoped one-time token (scope + ttl), 3) telemetry gating so shadow can be promoted only if predefined metrics stay within thresholds.

sasha: shadow-apply sounds great. question: should shadow be "sampled" (e.g. 5% of traffic) or full-sim with no effect? sampling reduces cost but may miss edge cases.

nina: ops/oncall here — sampling would hit 95% of usecases. main asks: easy rollback, clear audit trail, and SIEM integration (we push to Splunk).

liam: API suggestion:

```http
POST /v1/configs/apply
{ "id": "route_quota_v2", "mode": "shadow", "sample_percent": 5, "ttl": 3600 }
```

Response: { change_id, simulation_report_url }

jonah: server-side contract: the simulation must exercise the identical evaluation path as real apply (same selector code and decision tree). otherwise shadow is useless.

sasha: agree. simulation should also produce a compare diff: which requests would have been routed differently, expected quota hits, and any predicted latency delta. for telemetry cost control, sample only a small percent of actual evals.

maya: ops-bot should emit lifecycle events for creation/promotion/expiry. ops-bot: any constraints?

ops-bot: auto: created shadow-run change_id=chg_2026_0047 for route_quota_v2, mode=shadow, sample=5%, expires in 3600s. Link: https://console.redwood/shadow/chg_2026_0047 :robot_face: 

nina: delegation tokens must be bound to an incident tag (e.g., incident-1234) and require manual approval for TTL > 30m. also require reason field for audit.

liam: edge case: shadow touches multiple interdependent flags (route + quota + cache ttl). we need atomic simulation across deps or the diff is misleading.

jonah: we can run the simulation transactionally but not commit; produce per-service diffs and a global summary. add an activation_policy field: manual | auto-promote-on-metrics | timed.

sasha: telemetry gating: recommend default metric set: error_rate (5xx), p50_latency, kv_miss_99p. default thresholds but allow per-change overrides. also emit change-level anomaly scores.

maya: UX: console should show shadow vs live decision side-by-side, highlighted risky traces, and an obvious "promote to staging" -> "promote to live" path with approval checks.

liam: audit schema: who delegated, who used token, change snapshot, who promoted, chain-of-approval. store signed snapshots in WAL and link to SIEM.

jonah: security: delegation tokens must be single-use, KMS-backed, rotateable, and auditable. private-deploy customers should be able to opt-out of auto-telemetry sampling.

nina: +1 on pilot. we should run with two teams: oncall + platform to validate edge cases and training materials.

maya: agreed. action items: jonah -> proto API for shadow/apply, sasha -> simulation hooks and compare diff, liam -> audit + token flow, nina -> pilot coordination + SIEM mapping. i'll write a short RFC and include examples.
